findings.title: Audit log GET always dereferences member.has_global_access
findings.body: Every audit-log GET now evaluates `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` before pagination, even when `optimized_pagination` is absent. `organization_context.member` is an RPC member and can be null (for example a superuser is short-circuited, but any non-superuser request with no member object is not). `has_global_access` is a Django OrganizationMember property, not a field on the RPC member. If the attribute is missing or member is None, this raises AttributeError and the entire audit log endpoint returns 500 for ordinary callers.

findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
findings.body: When `optimized_pagination=true` and the caller is a superuser or has global access, the endpoint switches from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator while still passing `order_by="-datetime"`. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py around line 840) does math.floor/math.ceil on the model attribute. For AuditLogEntry that attribute is a datetime, so the first page that has rows raises TypeError while building the next cursor. value_from_cursor also returns the raw numeric cursor instead of a timezone-aware datetime, so any later page would compare a timestamp column to an integer and fail in Postgres. The new path is unusable for this endpoint.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets intentionally bypass pagination bounds
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator, enabled on the org audit-log endpoint by the client-controlled `optimized_pagination=true` query param plus `enable_advanced_features=True`, feeds a negative cursor offset straight into queryset slicing. The comments state this is meant to read data beyond normal pagination bounds. Other paginators in this file reject a negative offset with BadPaginationError; this one special-cases it. Django QuerySet slicing raises ValueError on a negative start, so the path 500s today rather than returning extra rows, but the client supplies the cursor (`value:offset:is_prev`) and a slice implementation that accepts negative indexes would return rows outside the cursor window. BasePaginator.get_result (line 182) was also changed so previous-page cursors keep a negative offset on every endpoint that uses it. This is an unrelated bound-bypass and should not be merged.

findings.title: Set keys switched to sorted sets with no migration
findings.body: Span buffer keys `span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id` were Redis SETs (SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN) and are now sorted sets (ZADD here, ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN in add-buffer.lua, ZSCAN in _load_segment_data). The key format is unchanged and nothing deletes or converts existing keys. After deploy, any in-flight segment still stored as a SET makes those commands fail with WRONGTYPE, so process_spans errors and those traces are not buffered until the key expires (redis_ttl defaults to 3600s). A rollback is equally broken: once a new process ZADDs a key, the old SADD/SSCAN code also gets WRONGTYPE. Mixed-version deploys cannot drain the buffer.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM corrupts end-timestamp scores
findings.body: Merging segment keys now uses ZUNIONSTORE with the default AGGREGATE SUM (both the span_key merge at this line and the parent_key merge just below). Members are span payloads and scores are end_timestamp_precise, used later by ZPOPMIN to decide which spans to drop. Redis sums scores when the same payload is in both keys. That overlap happens on Kafka redelivery: the span is ZADDed onto the grouped parent key in process_spans and is still present in the previous segment key that this script unions in. The summed score is no longer an end timestamp, so eviction keeps the redelivered span and drops a different span whose real timestamp is older. SUNIONSTORE used to dedupe without changing identity. The union needs AGGREGATE MIN or MAX so the score stays a timestamp.

findings.title: Insert-time ZPOPMIN can drop the root span silently
findings.body: Once a segment sorted set exceeds 1000 members, the script ZPOPMINs the lowest end_timestamp scores down to 1000. The root/segment span is not protected, and the has-root-span flag is set independently of whether that payload is still in the set. A root that ended before its children, or any span that loses the score tie-break, is deleted and never flushed, while the segment still looks complete downstream and may still use the shorter root timeout. The flush-time guard in _load_segment_data that skipped segments over max_segment_spans (1001) and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded was removed, and the 1000 cap is hardcoded in Lua rather than passed from SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans. Oversized segments that miss this script (WRONGTYPE, script error, crash between the earlier ZADD and EVALSHA) are now flushed in full with no metric. Drops are silent.

findings.title: Redirect walk cap cut from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The parent-redirect walk that finds the segment key used to run up to 10000 hops, with a comment that a chain past that limit would not be joined correctly. It is now 1000, and the comment is gone. Each span adds a redirect entry. A parent chain longer than 1000 stops early, hsets the new span to an intermediate id, and merges into the wrong set. Those spans are flushed as a separate or truncated segment instead of the real trace segment, with no error.

findings.title: No coverage for eviction, score merges, or the new paginator
findings.body: Existing buffer tests only insert a handful of spans, all with the same end_timestamp_precise, and still only assert the full segment is flushed. Nothing covers a segment over 1000 spans, ZPOPMIN dropping or preserving the root, ZUNIONSTORE score behavior on redelivery, or WRONGTYPE against a leftover SET key. The audit-log OptimizedCursorPaginator path and negative-offset cursor handling also have no tests, so the datetime crash and bound-bypass path would ship green.

findings.title: Buffer docstring still describes Redis sets
findings.body: The module glossary and the insert steps still say span-buf:s:* keys are sets and that payloads are added to a set. They are sorted sets scored by end_timestamp_precise, trimmed with ZPOPMIN. Operators debugging Redis or a flush incident will run SET commands (SMEMBERS/SCARD) and get WRONGTYPE, and the docstring no longer mentions that spans above 1000 are discarded on insert.
